newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 6-yr high on bullish economy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 6-yr high on bullish economy.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed at a six-year high in frantic trade on Friday, reflecting a bullish economic outlook following the announcement of high gross domestic product growth for the fourh quarter, brokers said.
The weighted index climbed 113.15 points or 1.47 percent to end at 7,791.19, surpassing the 7,687.28 finish on Monday and marking the market's highest close since ending at 7,857.01 on June 2, 1990.
Turnover was a frantic T$166.9 billion ($6.05 billion). That exceeded the T$156.99 billion on Wednesday and marked the highest total since T$185.9 billion on January 6, 1994.
The government announced on Thursday that Taiwan's GDP for the fourth quarter of 1996 was 6.62 percent, higher than a forecast of 6.58 percent.
It also raised its GDP prediction for 1997 to 6.28 percent from 6.20 percent.
"Investors are very optimistic about the economy, and their confidence continues to boost the market," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
"The general expectation is for the economy to reach its peak in the second half of this year, and the stock market likely would react a little earlier," Fang said.
Textiles saw late buying push their index up 3.17 percent. Both Universal Textile and Everest Textile soared by the daily seven-percent limit or T$1.70 to T$26.
Fundamentals-backed electronics continued their recent bull run, with the sector closing 2.23 percent higher.
Brokers expected the index to slip slightly on Saturday before trying to break the 7,800-level resistance. A 7,730-7,800 range was seen. -- Kevin Chen (2-5080815)
